citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Daily observation of three rabbits was not done sufficiently to assess their health and well-being.
- A white rabbit with black spots along the spine and over the face as well as black ears was seen with a circular firm
mass, approximately 1 inch in diameter, on the neck below the left ear. The hair at the intersection between the neck and
the mass was thinning/parting revealing a small circular red and yellow ulcerated lesion.
- A small fuzzy grey kit was seen with a large amount of debris, hair and hay coating the area where the eyes should be.
There was a large amount of thick sticky cloudy white material gluing the hay and debris onto the right eye. A facility
representative removed the debris from both eyes allowing them to open. Both eyes were small and cloudy white/grey in
color with reddened hairless eyelids around.
- A white rabbit was seen laying down at the corner of the enclosure with his head tilted down towards the left side. The tilt
remained when the rabbit moved around and at times quick twitching right eye movements were seen.
The licensee had not identified the conditions affecting these animals, therefore had not contacted the veterinarian for
guidance on care. Failure to promptly identify animal conditions delays treatment which may negatively impact animal
health and comfort. A more rigorous method of daily observation of all animals must be implemented to properly assess
their health and well-being. Direct and frequent communication with the attending veterinarian is required for timely
diagnosis and adequate medical attention. The veterinarian needs to be consulted regarding the currently affected
animals to obtain an appropriate diagnosis and treatment plan. Correct by August 28, 2026.

Approximately 20 Syrian hamster enclosures were in need of repair and contained sharp points that could result in animal
injury. Varying amounts of damage were seen affecting the metal lixit (only source of water) as well as the circular metal
grommets covering the plastic hole that allows access to the lixit. The damage created sharp points within direct contact
of the animals. Animals coming in contact with sharp points when drinking from the lixit could suffer injury. Housing
facilities must be structurally sound and maintained in good repair, to protect the animals from injury. Correct by
September 18, 2026.

Twenty-five enclosures, each housing two rabbits, had inadequate floor space in accordance with the AWA and
regulations. The enclosures were either 2 feet long and 1 ft wide (2 square feet) or 2 ft long and 15 inches wide (2.5
square feet). Rabbits such as these weighing less than 4.4 pounds need to have 1.5 square feet each of available floor
space. Therefore, enclosures housing two rabbits need to provide a minimum of 3 square feet of floor space. Adequate
floor space is necessary to allow the rabbits to make normal postural and social adjustments with adequate freedom of
movement. Per a facility representative, the rabbits pair housed as described above, were done so for a period of 24
hours for breeding. Regardless of the timeframe, each rabbit weighing less than 4.4lbs shall be provided with 1.5 square
feet of space. Correct by September 11, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Lisa Ekman, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
